below, landing approximately two meters from a mechanic who was grinding at deck level. The ring then bounced 
and struck the mechanic on the arm. The mechanic received a first-aid level impact with no observable injury. The 
event had a severe potential for fatality due to the weight and fall height. The ring had been brought into the elevated 
work area earlier than planned, the area was insufficiently barricaded, and the test occurred without notification to 
the crew below. Multiple procedural, communication and barrier-management weaknesses contributed.

An employee was standing behind a winch truck. The truck rolled back and ran over the employee's left leg. The employee suffered a thigh injury, a head laceration, and bruising to the right-side ribs.

Pressure safety valve released on low pressure sweep line.

inspection of the area, a vapor cloud and condensate leak were identified in Unit-84 from the Slug Catcher Filter 
area, (2’’ Line at upstream of 84-BDV-01.19).
Shift Supervisor/MCR Panel were immediately informed about the leak. The operator pulled the MAC, activated the 
deluge system, and provided a water curtain as per the Shift Supervisor’s direction. Plant emergency shutdown was 
initiated; the leaking section was isolated by closing ESVs and depressurized through the PCV on the Pre-Flash 
Drum to flare.
On inspection, a major hole, around 3” equivalent leak size was identified upstream of BDV01.19.
This leak triggered a Tier-2 Emergency Response, with personnel evacuating. 70 personnel were evaluated by the 
medical team, with toxic clips detecting 5ppm H2S at an occupied area, ~1.3Km away from the leak location. Of the 
personnel evaluated for gas exposure, 29 were classified as First Aid cases.

Two operators were preparing the well (gas lift) for maintenance. During preparation, the operators were supposed

A severe industrial accident occurred on an offshore production platform during gas import operations. At the 
time, the platform was in the process of decommissioning, with most production systems already shut down and 
being readied for dismantling; only the gas import line remained operational to supply the power generator. On 
the morning of the incident, this last active pipeline ruptured after years of progressive corrosion, which developed 
specifically on its upper surface - an area exposed to salty water dripping through an unsealed opening between 
decks directly above. Because the line was installed in an elevated position, the most recent inspections did not fully 
address the upper side, allowing a localized, severe corrosion spot on the top of the pipe to go undetected. When the 
rupture finally occurred, a large volume of flammable gas was released and quickly ignited, resulting in a powerful 
jet fire and vapor cloud explosion. Multiple workers were injured, rescue efforts were hampered by equipment 
failures and communication problems, and the event resulted in significant material damage and evacuation of the 
platform.
